title: MUST y HAVE TO
subtitle: Must and have to · obligación y prohibición

map.center: Usamos MUST y HAVE TO para decir lo que tenemos que hacer: normas y obligaciones.

explain.es: Must y have to significan tener que / deber: obligaciones y normas del cole, de casa… ¡Pero sus negativas son muy diferentes! mustn't = ¡prohibido! y don't have to = no hace falta.
explain.en: Must and have to = it's necessary. But mustn't = not allowed and don't have to = not necessary.

explain.title: 1 · MUST
explain.es: Must + verbo (¡sin to!) es una obligación fuerte: cuando yo creo que algo es muy importante y en normas escritas (carteles). Must es perezoso: nunca cambia (sin -s, sin do / does).
explain.en: Must + verb (no to) = strong obligation: our own idea or written rules. It never changes.
formula: I / you / he / she / we / they + *must* + verbo

examples.es: Tengo que ordenar mi cuarto hoy.

examples.en: You must wear a helmet on your bike.
examples.es: Debes llevar casco en la bici.
Lucía tiene que estudiar para su examen.

explain.title: 2 · HAVE TO / HAS TO
explain.es: Have to también significa tener que. Lo usamos sobre todo cuando la obligación viene de fuera: una norma del cole, un horario, lo que dicen papá y mamá. ¡Ojo! Have to sí cambia: con he, she, it se convierte en has to.
explain.en: Have to also means something is necessary, often because of rules or other people. With he, she, it we say has to.
formula: I / you / we / they + *have to* + verbo

examples.en: I have to get up at seven on school days.
examples.es: Tengo que levantarme a las siete los días de cole.

examples.en: Mario has to walk Rocky every evening.
examples.es: Mario tiene que pasear a Rocky todas las tardes.

examples.en: We have to wear a uniform at school.
examples.es: Tenemos que llevar uniforme en el cole.

explain.title: MUST o HAVE TO
explain.es: En frases afirmativas, must y have to significan casi lo mismo y muchas veces sirven los dos. La pequeña diferencia es quién pone la norma: ¿lo pienso yo o viene de fuera?
explain.en: In positive sentences, must and have to are very similar. The small difference is who makes the rule.

cols.head: 🗣️ Lo pienso yo · must
items: I must call Grandma. (Yo creo que es importante.)

cols.head: 📋 Norma de fuera · have to
items: I have to wear glasses. (Lo dice el médico.)
We have to be at school at nine.

explain.title: 3 · MUSTN'T
explain.es: Mustn't (= must not) significa ¡prohibido! ¡No lo hagas! Es una luz roja 🔴. Fíjate en cómo se dice: la primera t no suena → /ˈmʌsnt/. Tampoco aquí cambia nada con he / she / it.
explain.en: Mustn't (= must not) means it is not allowed. Don't do it! The first t is silent.

examples.es: No debes correr por el pasillo.

examples.en: We mustn't use our phones in class.
examples.es: No podemos usar el móvil en clase.

examples.en: Rocky mustn't eat chocolate. It's bad for dogs!
examples.es: Rocky no debe comer chocolate. ¡Es malo para los perros!

explain.title: 4 · DON'T HAVE TO
explain.title_en: Don't have to: it isn't necessary
explain.es: Don't have to / doesn't have to significa no hace falta, no es obligatorio. Puedes hacerlo si quieres, pero no es necesario. Es una luz verde 🟢: ¡tú eliges! Como have to es un verbo normal, la negativa se hace con don't / doesn't.
explain.en: Don't have to means it is not necessary. You can do it if you want, but you don't need to. Use don't / doesn't.
formula: I / you / we / they + *don't have to* + verbo
he / she / it + *doesn't have to* + verbo

examples.en: It's Saturday! I don't have to get up early.
You don't have to pay. The museum is free.
examples.es: No hace falta pagar. El museo es gratis.

examples.en: Lucía doesn't have to wear a uniform at her new school.
examples.es: Lucía no tiene que llevar uniforme en su cole nuevo.

explain.title: MUSTN'T o DON'T HAVE TO
explain.es: ¡Aquí está la gran trampa! En español «no tienes que…» puede sonar a las dos cosas, pero en inglés son muy diferentes. Pregúntate: ¿está prohibido o simplemente no hace falta?
explain.en: This is the big trap! Mustn't = it's forbidden. Don't have to = it isn't necessary, you choose.

cols.head: 🟢 No hace falta · don't have to
items: You don't have to swim. (Si no quieres, no.)
You don't have to help me. (Puedo solo.)
You don't have to bring food. (Hay comida.)

explain.title: 5 · Preguntas
explain.es: Para preguntar si algo es obligatorio usamos Do / Does + sujeto + have to + verbo? Respondemos con do / does, igual que en el presente simple. (Must I…? existe, pero es más formal y se usa poco.)
explain.en: To ask about obligation: Do / Does + subject + have to + verb? Short answers: Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't.
formula: *Do* + I / you / we / they + *have to* + verbo?

examples.en: Do we have to do this exercise? — Yes, you do.
Does Leo have to go home now? — No, he doesn't.
examples.es: ¿Leo tiene que irse a casa ya? — No.

examples.en: Do you have to feed the cat? — Yes, I do.
examples.es: ¿Tienes que dar de comer al gato? — Sí.

items.es: ¿Lo piensas tú o es un cartel? → must. ¿Es una norma de fuera (cole, padres, horario)? → have to.
items.en: Your idea or a sign → must. A rule from outside → have to.

items.es: ¿No hace falta y puedes elegir? 🟢 → don't / doesn't have to.
items.en: Not necessary? → don't / doesn't have to.

items.es: Mira el sujeto: con he / she / it → has to / doesn't have to. ¡Must no cambia nunca!
items.en: he / she / it → has to / doesn't have to. Must never changes.

items.es: Detrás va el verbo en su forma base: must go, has to go, doesn't have to go.
items.en: Then the base verb: must go, has to go.

lines.en: Welcome to camp, Mario! Here are the rules.
lines.es: ¡Bienvenido al campamento, Mario! Aquí tienes las normas.

lines.en: Do we have to get up early?
Yes, we do. We have to be at breakfast at eight.
lines.es: Sí. Tenemos que estar en el desayuno a las ocho.

lines.en: Oh no! And what about phones?
We mustn't use our phones during the day, only after dinner.
lines.es: No podemos usar el móvil durante el día, solo después de cenar.

lines.en: Do I have to swim in the lake? I don't like cold water!
lines.es: ¿Tengo que nadar en el lago? ¡No me gusta el agua fría!

lines.en: No, you don't have to. But you must wear a life jacket in the boat!
lines.es: No, no hace falta. ¡Pero tienes que llevar chaleco salvavidas en la barca!

explain.title: Truco del semáforo
explain.es: 🔴 mustn't = luz roja: ¡STOP, prohibido! · 🟢 don't have to = luz verde: tú decides, no hace falta. · must / have to = ¡hay que hacerlo! Y recuerda: must no tiene pasado. Para ayer usamos had to: Yesterday I had to study.
explain.en: 🔴 mustn't = stop, not allowed. 🟢 don't have to = you choose. Must / have to = you need to do it. Past: had to.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el texto. Marca T (true, verdadero) o F (false, falso) y contesta las preguntas.
exercises.en: Read the text. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: Hi! I'm Mario. My school has got a lot of rules. We have to be at school at nine o'clock, and we mustn't be late. We have to wear a uniform: a blue jumper and grey trousers. But on Fridays we don't have to wear the uniform. We can wear our own clothes!

In class, we must put our hands up to speak, and we mustn't use our phones. My sister Lucía is at secondary school. She doesn't have to wear a uniform, but she has to do a lot of homework. And me? Every evening I have to walk Rocky, our dog. I don't mind. I love it!

items.q: Mario has to be at school at nine o'clock.
Mario has to wear a uniform on Fridays.
items.why: On Fridays he doesn't have to wear the uniform.

items.q: Pupils can use their phones in class.
Does Lucía have to wear a uniform?
What does Lucía have to do?
items.a: She has to do a lot of homework.

items.q: What does Mario have to do every evening?
items.a: He has to walk Rocky (the dog).
